key_insight: Prompts can systematically override visual evidence in large vision-language models (LVLMs), producing prompt-induced hallucinations; HalluScope quantifies and characterizes how different prompt types and model components drive these failures.
problem_solved: Clarifies and measures the extent to which prompts (rather than vision backbones alone) cause LVLMs to hallucinate, providing a reproducible benchmark to compare models and mitigation strategies.
method: Construct HalluScope: a controlled benchmark of images paired with neutral, leading, and adversarial prompts to elicit potential hallucinations.
Evaluate multiple state-of-the-art LVLMs across prompt conditions, measuring hallucination frequency, severity, and types (e.g., object insertion, attribute fabrication, false relations).
Analyze correlations between prompt characteristics, language-model dominance, and vision-backbone limitations to identify when and why prompts override visual grounding.
impact: Gives practitioners a practical tool and evidence-based guidance to detect, compare, and reduce prompt-induced hallucinations in LVLM deployments, improving reliability for vision-grounded applications.
visual_elements: Side-by-side example: image + neutral prompt vs leading prompt with the two model outputs annotated (ground-truth vs hallucination).
Bar chart: hallucination rate by model and prompt type (neutral / leading / adversarial).
Pipeline flowchart: HalluScope generation → evaluation metrics → taxonomy of hallucination types.
Heatmap or scatter: relationship between prompt strength and severity of hallucination across models.
paper_title: When Prompts Override Vision: Prompt-Induced Hallucinations in LVLMs
paper_authors: Pegah Khayatan, Jayneel Parekh, Arnaud Dapogny, Mustafa Shukor, Alasdair Newson
